key_insight: A shared, foundation-style PV forecasting model enables zero-shot deployment at unseen stations, reducing the need for separate site-specific models.
engineering_relevance: The framework could simplify forecasting deployment and maintenance across distributed PV fleets while supporting later adaptation to local operating needs.
method: Pretrain on heterogeneous multi-site, multi-horizon PV data.
Treat forecasting as sequence completion using PV history, weather observations, future numerical weather predictions, and time encodings.
Combine forecast-aligned and random reconstruction objectives for balanced accuracy, weather-input robustness, and adaptation.
evidence_signal: Experiments used 479 PV stations—340 for development and 139 spatially held out for zero-shot evaluation—with reported gains over site-specific, shared, and generalist time-series baselines across 6-hour to 7-day horizons.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify accuracy gains or deployment costs, leaving operational value and resource requirements to be verified.
paper_title: Foundation-Style Pretraining for Scalable and Transferable Distributed PV Forecasting
